phases.title: Survival
phases.goal: Greet people, introduce yourself and handle basic transactions with memorised chunks.
can: Pronounce the German sounds: ä/ö/ü umlauts, ß, ch (ich vs. ach), and the rolled/uvular r
Use greetings and courtesies: Hallo, Guten Tag, Tschüss, bitte, danke, Entschuldigung
Count 0–20 and give your name, nationality and where you live (Ich heiße…, Ich komme aus…)
Conjugate sein and haben in the present (ich bin/du bist, ich habe/du hast)
Recognise that every noun has a gender (der/die/das) and is written with a capital letter
Order food and shop with Ich hätte gern… and Was kostet das?
phases.daily: 10 min pronunciation drills (umlauts + ch), 10 min flashcards for greetings & numbers, 5 min saying your self-introduction aloud.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.goal: Build correct present-tense sentences and start using the two most common cases.
can: Conjugate regular -en verbs in all six persons plus stem-changers (fahren→fährst, lesen→liest)
Master the nominative and accusative cases, including der→den for masculine objects
Negate correctly with nicht (for verbs/adjectives) and kein/keine (for nouns)
Use the accusative prepositions durch, für, gegen, ohne, um
Keep the verb in second position (V2) and invert after a fronted time/place phrase
Tell the time and use numbers to 100 in shopping and appointments
phases.daily: 15 min verb-conjugation practice, 10 min case drills (nom vs. akk), 10 min listening to slow German dialogues, 5 min writing three sentences.

phases.title: Core Structures
phases.goal: Speak about the past and connect ideas with subordinate clauses.
can: Form the Perfekt with haben/sein + Partizip II and choose the right auxiliary
Use modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen…) with the infinitive pushed to the end
Split separable verbs correctly (Ich rufe dich an) in main clauses
Master the dative case and its prepositions (aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu)
Build subordinate clauses with weil, dass, wenn — sending the verb to the end
Handle the two-way prepositions with accusative for motion, dative for location
phases.daily: 15 min Perfekt & modal practice, 10 min dative/two-way preposition drills, 15 min graded reading, 10 min speaking about your day in the past tense.

phases.title: Fluency
phases.goal: Express nuance with adjective endings, comparisons, the passive and relative clauses.
can: Apply strong, weak and mixed adjective endings by gender, case and article
Form comparatives and superlatives (größer als, am schnellsten) including irregulars
Use the genitive case and its prepositions (wegen, während, trotz)
Build the passive with werden + Partizip II across tenses
Connect ideas with relative clauses (der/die/das … Verb at the end)
Use um…zu and infinitive-with-zu constructions to express purpose and opinions
phases.daily: 10 min adjective-ending drills, 20 min podcasts or news at natural speed, 15 min conversation with a partner/tutor, 10 min keeping a short German journal.

phases.title: Mastery
phases.goal: Use the full tense and mood system naturally and adapt register to any situation.
can: Narrate in the Präteritum (war, ging, kam) as used in writing and storytelling
Use the Plusquamperfekt with nachdem for sequencing past events
Express hypotheticals and politeness with Konjunktiv II (wäre, hätte, würde, könnte)
Report speech with Konjunktiv I (er sei, sie habe) in formal contexts
Deploy Futur I and modal particles (doch, mal, ja, halt) for natural nuance
Switch fluidly between formal Sie and informal du and follow regional accents
phases.daily: 30 min native media (books, films, Tagesschau), 20 min writing essays or emails, active use of new idioms in conversation, and self-correction of the subjunctive.
